output: Muhammad Qutb (1906-1996) was an Egyptian Islamic scholar, author, and the father of Islamist thinker Sayyid Qutb. He was a leading figure in the Muslim Brotherhood and a major influence on the development of Islamist thought. He was imprisoned by the Egyptian government for his political views and later exiled to the United States, where he taught at the University of Northern Colorado. He is best known for his book Fi Zilal al-Quran (In the Shade of the Quran), which is widely considered to be one of the most important works of Islamic literature.

input: Question: Tell me a bio of Cicero.
output: Cicero was a Roman statesman, orator, and philosopher. He was born in 106 BCE in Arpinum, a small town in the Apennine foothills of central Italy. He was educated in Rome, where he became an accomplished orator and gained a reputation for his ability to speak and reason. He was an outspoken critic of the Roman dictator Julius Caesar, and was eventually assassinated for his opposition to Caesar's regime. He is remembered as one of the greatest orators and political theorists of the ancient world.

He was known for his aggressive and unpredictable playing style. He retired from competitive chess in 1992, but continued to make headlines with his controversial statements. He died in Iceland in 2008.

input: Question: Tell me a bio of Henry VII of England.
output: Henry VII (1457-1509) was the King of England from 1485 to 1509. He was the founder of the Tudor dynasty and was the first monarch of the House of Tudor. He was the son of Edmund Tudor, 1st Earl of Richmond, and Margaret Beaufort. He was crowned King of England in 1485 after defeating Richard III at the Battle of Bosworth Field. He was an effective ruler, restoring order to the country after the Wars of the Roses. He also strengthened the monarchy by introducing the concept of the royal prerogative. He was a successful diplomat, negotiating the Treaty of Etaples with France in 1492. He was also an able administrator, reforming the legal system and introducing the first permanent standing army in England. He was succeeded by his son, Henry VIII.

Himmler was a loyal follower of Adolf Hitler and was one of the few people who knew about the Führer's plans for the extermination of the Jews. He was captured by the Allies in 1945 and committed suicide while in custody.

output: Griselda Blanco was a Colombian drug lord and pioneer in the Miami-based cocaine trade. She was known as the "Godmother of Cocaine" and was one of the most powerful and ruthless drug lords of the 1970s and 1980s. She was responsible for the spread of cocaine across the United States and was involved in numerous murders and assassinations. She was eventually arrested in 1985 and sentenced to 20 years in prison, but was released in 2004 and deported to Colombia.
